positioning: The smartest dog in the room, and it knows it.
story: The Border Collie is widely called the most intelligent breed alive. It has the work ethic to back the claim.
It was bred in the border hills between England and Scotland to herd sheep. It does so with an uncanny, crouching stare known as the eye. A whole flock bends to it.
The mind is startling. A Border Collie named Chaser learned the names of more than a thousand objects. She could fetch each one on command.
That brilliance is a responsibility. A Border Collie needs a job, hard exercise, and a problem to solve every day. A bored one will invent work. Children, cars, and shadows are all fair game.
The breed excels at nearly everything. It dominates herding trials, agility, and flying-disc contests. The AKC recognized it in 1995, long after shepherds had settled its reputation.
For the right person it is unmatched. Devoted, sensitive, and tuned to every signal. Give it a task and a partner and you have the finest working mind in dogdom.
rank_cap: Widely called the world’s smartest breed (AKC)
fblocks: Named for the border country between England and Scotland. Collie is an old word for the herding dogs of the British hills.
Routinely ranked the most intelligent breed. Chaser learned over a thousand object names, a record for a dog.
Built to work all day. Without a job and hard exercise it grows anxious and destructive. Needs an active owner.
A low, crouching stare steers livestock without force. Pet Border Collies will herd people and pets alike.
Recognized by the AKC in 1995. Four to eight puppies to a litter. Champion of herding trials and most dog sports.
days: Peat smoke, a dented kettle, and an old dog who has finally been told he can stop.
The eye is a low, hard stare. A Border Collie can steer a flock without a bark.
Chaser learned the names of more than a thousand toys. She could fetch each one by name.
Border Collies herd without being asked. Ducks, children, and the occasional lawnmower.
Sit still on the machine. Watch the whole hill. Decide before you move.
The breed is named for the border country between England and Scotland.
Eight puppies tumble over one patient old dog. He is too kind to stand up.
last_walk:
The lantern is low, and the lambing shed is quiet.
Fly lies in the straw. A newborn lamb sleeps against her warm side. She has been up all night. She will be up again tomorrow. A Border Collie’s work is never really done. But for one hour, in lantern light, keeping watch is enough.
